title: Mark of Destiny
next_chapter_hook: The characters on the stone tablet seemed to come alive, writhing before Chen Ji's eyes—Chapter 700: Finale. This wasn't prophecy; this was a script. Who, and where, had written the road he hadn't yet walked?

text.content: That will was as heavy as substance. Chen Ji felt his soul being dissected and examined inch by inch. Not the probing techniques of Tianqing Sect, not the aura of the Demonic Path, not any detection method he had ever read about in ancient texts. This was a gaze that transcended the boundaries of his understanding—as if a pair of eyes were descending from extremely high and far, pinning his entire being onto the chessboard of destiny. The fragment at his chest grew faintly warm, a temperature he had never felt while conscious.

Ye Qing's face turned deathly pale in an instant. Her Demonic Path mist instinctively surged out, yet it dissolved like thin paper meeting boiling water, unable to form any concealment. She gritted her teeth and murmured: "This isn't an ordinary secret realm prohibition—that will, I once saw descriptions of in the sacred texts—is... the Eye of Heavenly Dao." Her voice on the last word was almost挤出 from between her teeth, filled with disbelief that even she couldn't fathom.

dialogue.content: "Impossible... How could the fate observation device that our Demonic Path has searched for three hundred years be here?"

text.content: Chen Ji didn't respond to Ye Qing's words. His entire attention was drawn to the light rising from beneath his feet. Pale golden patterns spread from the base of the stone tablet, crawling onto his boots like living creatures, ascending along his meridians. It wasn't binding; it felt more like... registration. His Tianji Record fragment trembled violently at the same moment, two forces of the same origin beginning to resonate across the void. A blurry image flashed through his mind—innumerable points of light scattered across the mortal world, each connected by a thread as fine as a strand of hair.

The text on the stone tablet began to transform. Not carved, but manifesting凭空, jumping out one character at a time like movable type. Chen Ji recognized those characters—precisely the primordial seal script he had seen on the back of the Tianji Record fragment, though no one had ever translated them. He had barely managed to recognize them through the sporadic guidance of Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul. The first word to appear was: Spectator. Immediately following was: Seventh Hundred and Thirty-Second Generation. The third line of text made Chen Ji's pupils contract sharply—Tianji Record Keeper.

dialogue.content: "(Tianji Record Keeper... the user of the Tianji Record?)"

text.content: The stone tablet seemed to hear his inner voice. The fourth line slowly appeared: Number—Tianji Record_ch0023. Chen Ji's blood seemed to freeze at that moment. Twenty-three. This was the number of the fragment he had inherited, information Mo Xiansheng had never mentioned. The Tianji Record wasn't the only one. There had been more than one Record Keeper across the ages. And now, his name, his identity, his bond with the Tianji Record—all had been recorded by this secret realm, or rather, by that will currently gazing at him.

choice.prompt: Facing this truth sufficient to overturn his understanding, Chen Ji had to make a choice. Follow the trail to investigate thoroughly, or endure in silence and observe?

choices.description: Proactively touch the stone tablet to obtain more information about the Tianji Record's past Record Keepers and the fate observation device. Risk unknown, but may uncover earth-shattering secrets.
choices.risk_hint: The true purpose of the fate observation device remains unclear

text.content: Chen Ji raised his hand, fingertips touching the icy surface of the stone tablet. In that instant, a current of information like electricity surged into his Mental Sea—a sealed memory fragment from a former Record Keeper. The images were fragmented, but sufficient for him to see: across the long ages, the Tianji Record had changed twenty-two masters, each walking a similar path—rising, scheming, reaching the summit, falling. And无一例外, their endings were all related to one phrase: Heavenly Fate Counterattack.

choices.description: Suppress the urge to investigate, memorize the stone tablet's contents, then withdraw from its sensing range. Observe first, then judge. Safe but may miss key information.
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing may have independent discoveries

text.content: Chen Ji slowly drew back his hand, stepping backward. His expression remained calm, as if what he had just seen was merely boring stone carvings. But his right hand had already secretly clenched, fingernails deeply embedded in his palm. That wasn't anger; it was a reminder—I've noted it. Twenty-three Record Keepers, twenty-three types of death. This road, predecessors have walked it. No reference value, but cautionary significance. He took a deep breath, turning to Ye Qing: "What does your Demonic Path want with the fate observation device?"

Ye Qing's voice grew hoarse. Her gaze remained on those faintly visible characters on the stone tablet: "The sacred texts record that the Eye of Heavenly Dao is not invincible. It's merely an... observation mechanism, used to ensure fate's trajectory follows certain preset patterns. And the fate observation device is one of its eyes placed in the mortal realm. If we can find it, destroy it, we can sever its monitoring of certain regions. The Demonic Path began searching three hundred years ago, but always found nothing." She smiled bitterly, "Who would have thought it was right here, in the Back Mountain of Tianqing Sect."

Chen Ji silently digested this information. The Eye of Heavenly Dao. Fate observation device. The resonance between Tianji Record and stone tablet. Mo Xiansheng never mentioned these—was it because he didn't know, or couldn't say? He suddenly recalled Mo Xiansheng's attitude each time he unsealed knowledge—only saying what should be said. So the question becomes: what should be said, and what shouldn't? Or rather, what does Mo Xiansheng himself not know? He raised his eyes toward a certain point in the void, as if to gaze into the eyes of that will observing him.

dialogue.content: "Interesting. So I thought I was the chess master, but in the end, I'm merely a piece recorded by the Spectator."

text.content: The text on the stone tablet suddenly trembled violently, as if sensing his emotions. Chen Ji's heart lurched—trouble. He wanted to retreat, but those pale golden patterns had already climbed to his wrist, gathering toward his chest. The Tianji Record fragment emitted a piercing hum at the same moment. The two forces began a dangerous fusion using him as the medium. Ye Qing cried out and lunged forward, her Demonic Path mist desperately surging, yet it struck an invisible wall.

choice.prompt: The Tianji Record and fate observation device have resonated. Chen Ji must decide quickly.

choices.description: Withstand the resonance impact using Heavenly Fate, forcefully sever the connection between the two. Cost: 5 points of Heavenly Fate, but can avoid unknown consequences.
choices.risk_hint: May draw the attention of the Eye of Heavenly Dao

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth, his consciousness plunging deep into his Mental Sea. He saw that fragment—now疯狂地 absorbing power flowing from the stone tablet, like a child starved for a thousand years. And those pale golden patterns were like needles, trying to pierce into the fragment's core. He didn't hesitate, directly detonating 5 points of Heavenly Fate. Agonizing pain exploded from the depths of his soul, yet the resonance was simultaneously severed. The fragment and stone tablet both quieted, leaving only a faint, sigh-like sound in the air.

choices.description: Risk allowing both to complete the resonance, using the fate observation device's power to glimpse more truth. Extremely high risk but may obtain key information.
choices.visible_cost: May be locked onto by the Eye of Heavenly Dao
choices.visible_reward: Glimpse the common fate of the Record Keepers
choices.risk_hint: Heavenly Fate Counterattack may trigger early

text.content: Chen Ji made a completely different choice. He didn't resist; instead, he proactively released control of the fragment, letting that pale golden power flood in. Two images unfolded simultaneously before his eyes—the left showing death records of past Record Keepers, the right showing the complete form of the fate observation device. They were a matching set. The Tianji Record was the key; the observation device was the keyhole. Whenever a Record Keeper used the Tianji Record's abilities, relevant information would automatically synchronize to this device. And the Eye of Heavenly Dao monitored all Record Keepers through it, ensuring no one could escape the chessboard.

No matter which method was chosen, the moment the resonance completely severed, the final line of text on the stone tablet appeared. Chen Ji's gaze, already turned away, was forcibly dragged back—those characters expanding in his pupils, expanding, until they occupied his entire field of vision. Pale golden light outlined seven characters, each stroke as clear as if carved by a knife: Chapter 700: Finale. These weren't ancient seal script, but modern cultivation world common characters he knew intimately. What did this mean? Chen Ji felt cold sweat seeping down his back.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji, what do you see? Your expression... is even more terrible than when the Eye of Heavenly Dao appeared."

text.content: Chen Ji didn't answer. His mind was racing at lightning speed. Chapter 700: Finale—the format of this phrase was too familiar. He had read countless story scripts, and every one had similar markers before the official chapter ended. And the Tianji Record was precisely what Mo Xiansheng called the "Chessboard Guardian." If the Tianji Record itself was a record of a book... if every step Chen Ji took, every choice he made, was merely a predetermined plotline in some grand narrative... then what did "Chapter 700: Finale" mean? The ending of this book? Or Chen Ji's death sentence? He slowly raised his head, gazing into the Eye of Heavenly Dao that might or might not exist in that void, the depths of his eyes churning with an unprecedented chill.

He suddenly laughed. It was an extremely complex laugh, containing self-mockery, anger, helplessness, and a trace of... liberation. Since it's a chess game, there must be a way to break the game. Since he's been recorded, that means there's still possibility for revision. In this life of his Chen Ji, walking from废物杂役 to today, which step wasn't a bloody path torn open from a dead end? Tianji Record Keeper? Observed piece? Fine, then let this chess game see when the piece can turn around and devour the chess player.

The text on the stone tablet began to fade, and that observing will receded like a tide. But before completely disappearing, Chen Ji clearly felt the final thread of information that will conveyed—not a threat, not a warning, but an almost playful... anticipation. Like a test-maker who had set重重关卡 was waiting for the test-taker to give an answer he hadn't anticipated. Ye Qing supported his swaying body, her voice urgent: "We must leave here. Though that will has retreated, it has remembered you—" Chen Ji waved his hand, interrupting her. His gaze finally swept across the stone tablet, silently noting that line's location in his heart. Chapter 700: Finale. He would find that finale.

And in that void above, at some unnameable place, an existence slowly withdrew its gaze. A pair of eyes condensed from pure Heavenly Dao laws blinked, as if appreciating a toy that was finally becoming interesting. Before it, an invisible book was automatically turning pages, stopping at the page marked "Tianji Record_ch0261." At the edge of the page, a line of small characters was faintly visible: Chapter 261: Mark of Destiny. And at the very bottom of this page, another line of characters was slowly forming—Next Chapter Preview: In Mo Xiansheng's silence, how many unspoken secrets lie hidden?
